messages:
Jordan (People Ops): Hey team — just got married in Spain last week! Want to add my spouse to benefits. They don't have an SSN yet (passport only) and our marriage certificate is the Spanish one (we're getting an English translation). Can I add them now for dental and vision and hold off on medical until SSN arrives? Also curious about HSA impact.
Sofia L.: Congrats! Quick answers: usually dental/vision are more flexible about SSNs, but medical carriers often want SSN for enrollment. Marriages are a QLE so you have 30 days from the event to submit docs for midyear enrollment.
Diego (Benefits): Adding detail: yes, you can usually enroll spouse for dental/vision as long as carrier accepts the foreign marriage cert + passport. For medical, carriers typically require either an SSN or an ITIN. If you don't have SSN yet, we can submit a `pending-ssn` request with passport + marriage cert + a signed affidavit saying SSN will be provided when available. Carrier responses vary.
Jordan (People Ops): If I enroll dental now and medical later, will premiums change or be prorated?
PayrollBot: Payroll note: mid-cycle additions are prorated. Premium deduction will start after carrier confirms effective date. Expect first deduction on next payroll after effective date; gross vs after-tax depends on benefit type.
Diego (Benefits): HSA note: If you add spouse to medical, your HSA contribution limits move from "individual" to "family" for IRS limits for the year. If you delay adding medical until later in the year, you'll remain under individual limits until effective date. We can update your HSA payroll contributions when medical becomes family coverage.
Sofia L.: Docs we need: 1) scanned marriage certificate (translated to English if not in English), 2) spouse passport copy, 3) proof of shared residence OR joint account (not always required but helpful), 4) SSN/ITIN when available. If you'll do dental now, indicate "dental only" in the subject line.
Jordan (People Ops): What's the secure upload method? I don't want to email passport scans.
Diego (Benefits): Use the secure HR portal link: https://hr.redwood.com/secure-upload (internal only). If you must email, use benefits@redwood.com but mark it as `SECURE` and we'll provide a transient upload link. Do not post scans in Slack.
Jordan (People Ops): Timeline expectations?
Diego (Benefits): Carrier turnaround typically 7-14 business days after complete docs. For QLE effective date: carrier rules usually set the effective date as the date of the QLE or first day of next month — it depends on carrier. We'll confirm the exact effective date when we submit.
Sofia L.: Action item for you: upload translated marriage cert + passport to the secure portal and open a ticket with subject `QLE - Add spouse (dental only)` if you want dental now. If you plan to add medical later, say so and include a note `SSN pending`. We'll tag payroll to prorate and HSA admin to adjust contribution caps when effective.
Jordan (People Ops): Thanks — uploading now. Appreciate the quick responses. :party_parrot:
